 3h ago 09.28 EDT 14th over: Sri Lanka 85-2 (Avishka Fernando 39, Rathnayake 25), target 430: A dismal souped-up version of Jennifer Rush’s dismal Power of Love is pumped over the PA as Dawson continues. Three singles are milked before Rathnayake pulls across the line with no little panache to punish a short ball and add four more.
 Share 3h ago 09.25 EDT 13th over: Sri Lanka 78-2 (Avishka Fernando 37, Rathnayake 20), target 430: “Make some noise!” yells the stadium announcer to the sparse crowd in the manner of a Waltzer operator on a fading seaside pier in February. But they have something to make some noise about when Rathnayake hooks Overton between fielders for a one-bounce four. Overton’s a bit awry here and follows it with a wide. He’s then taken for SIX as Rathnayake swings behind to fine leg – this partnership is beginning to bubble up.
 Share 3h ago 09.20 EDT 12th over: Sri Lanka 67-2 (Avishka Fernando 37, Rathnayake 10), target 430: A double change as Liam Dawson replaces Tongue to introduce spin for the first time. He’s pretty on the money, offering little width, and conceding four singles.
 Share 3h ago 09.17 EDT 11th over: Sri Lanka 63-2 (Avishka Fernando 35, Rathnayake 8), target 430: Jamie Overton comes into the attack, and Fernando clips an overpitched ball through midwicket for two. He adds a single before Rathnayake is kept honest by some decent length dot balls.
 Share 3h ago 09.14 EDT 10th over: Sri Lanka 60-2 (Avishka Fernando 32, Rathnayake 8), target 430: Sri Lanka pass 50 with a glorious six, flicked high and handsome into the crowd beyond square leg by Fernando, who threads a punchy drive through the gaps for four more three balls later. He’s playing some nice scoring strokes. A fifth of the way through the innings, Sri Lanka are just under an eighth of the way to the target.
 In South Africa, Scott Boland has been shifted at last! Australia seven down.
 South Africa v Australia: second men’s cricket Test, day five – live Read more Share 3h ago 09.09 EDT 9th over: Sri Lanka 49-2 (Avishka Fernando 22, Rathnayake 8), target 430: Fernando flicks Atkinson to leg for four more as on the Sky commentary they rue the lack of strike rotation. And there are far too many dots – some of it because it’s the power play but much of it due to a lack of nous and nimbleness. A rare single rounds off the over.
 Share Updated at  09.09 EDT 4h ago 09.05 EDT 8th over: Sri Lanka 44-2 (Avishka Fernando 17, Rathnayake 8), target 430: Rathnayake’s crouching low stance is reminiscent of a parent in a beach game, albeit much more effective, but it’s made to look ugly when Tongue cuts him in half with a beauty. It’s a fine maiden, the best over of the innings, and Sri Lanka are miles off the rate.
 Share Updated at  09.09 EDT 4h ago 09.01 EDT 7th over: Sri Lanka 44-2 (Avishka Fernando 17, Rathnayake 8), target 430: Sri Lanka overturn an lbw as Atkinson brings one in to Fernando, raps his pads, the finger goes up, the batter reviews – and DRS finds he nicked it. Fernando celebrates his reprieve with a hearty cut for four and a crisp straight drive for two.
 Share 4h ago 08.55 EDT 6th over: Sri Lanka 38-2 (Avishka Fernando 11, Rathnayake 8), target 430: England aren’t bowling that well to be honest, a bit too much loose and overpitched stuff, and one such is steered through extra cover for four to get Rathnayake off the mark. He repeats the feat off a better ball for four more.
 “The ODI batting of wristy maestros has come a long way from SM Gavaskar’s 36* (174) at Lord’s in 1975, eh?” I love the fact that of all Gavaskar’s achievements, that one remains so iconic.
 Share Updated at  08.57 EDT 4h ago 08.52 EDT 5th over: Sri Lanka 30-2 (Avishka Fernando 11, Rathnayake 0), target 430: Kusal Mendis, hero of Headingley last month, is the new man in, as Atkinson loses his radar and spears a wide down legside past Fernando – but his sprawling dive next ball effects the runout of Mendis . Fernando shows some defiance with a crisp cover drive for four, plus two more off the last ball.
 Share 4h ago 08.48 EDT Wicket! Kusal Mendis run out 0, SL 24-2
 Mendis is out without facing, as Atkinson deflects Fernando’s drive with the faintest of fingertips on to the stumps. Mendis is just about stranded and, after lengthy review, he has to go. When yer luck’s out, yer luck’s out.
 View image in fullscreen Sri Lanka's captain Kusal Mendis fails to reach his wicket. Photograph: Farooq Naeem/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  09.42 EDT 4h ago 08.43 EDT Wicket! Mendis b Tongue 18, Sri Lanka 23-1
 4th over: Sri Lanka 23-1 (Avishka Fernando 5), target 430: The first SIX of the innings comes with an effortless swivel-pull from Mendis off Tongue – he doesn’t need to hit it that high or hard, just use pure technique. But boundaries continue to be followed by dot balls as England keep control, a control enhanced when Tongue bowls Mendis with a delicious straightener off the last ball of the over . Big blow.
 View image in fullscreen Kamindu Mendis turns to see his bails tumble. Photograph: Anjum Naveed/AP Share Updated at  08.51 EDT 4h ago 08.38 EDT 3rd over: Sri Lanka 17-0 (Kamindu Mendis 12, Avishka Fernando 5), target 430: Fernando cracks Atkinson to deep backward point for a couple before essaying an unusual straight pull past mid-on for which they run two but could have had more. The pitch continues to look even and reliable for batters, and SL will be happy enough with how they’ve gone so far – just need to double the run rate. Easy.
 Share 4h ago 08.34 EDT 2nd over: Sri Lanka 13-0 (Kamindu Mendis 12, Avishka Fernando 1), target 430: Tongue, in for Sonny Baker, starts with a pleasing yorker to the right-handed Fernando, who’s off the mark with a single from the second ball. The ball’s coming nicely off Mendis’s bat and he square drives another boundary.
 “While this looks like a done deal, let us not forget that once Australia thought the same against South Africa way back in March 2006.” emails friend of the show Krishna Moorthy.
 Ah, great days. 
 Share Updated at  08.35 EDT 4h ago 08.30 EDT 1st over: Sri Lanka 8-0 (Kamindu Mendis 8, Avishka Fernando 0), target 430: As the sun sets over Rawalpindi, with the deweyness that entails, Gus Atkinson gets first use of the new ball, with which he sends down a gentle half-volley that Mendis creams through extra cover for four first ball. Four dots ensue before Mendis nudges down to fine leg for four more. Decent start in the circs for Sri Lanka – a mere 422 needed.
 Share 4h ago 08.25 EDT Before we focus on Sri Lanka’s reply , an update from St George’s Park where Australia are 245 fot 6 and Scott Boland leading the rearguard.
 South Africa v Australia: second men’s cricket Test, day five – live Read more Share Updated at  08.25 EDT 4h ago 08.21 EDT “That’s just silly,” emails Robert Wilson of Brook’s fireworks. “Plus, I actually thought his timing was a bit off. Might have been the mics but it didn’t quite sound like the full crack of felicitous contact. Imagine if he’d been on proper form. Double-plus, I’m still pretty sure I could do that. Under the right conditions*.
 *If I was batting against a team of six year olds*
 **Better make it five year olds.”
 Well yeah, that was the thing about that innings. Normally, the most striking (literally) aspect of Brook’s game is the forceful cleanness with which he hits the ball, bit this was all about agility, hand and wrist movement – perfect subcontinental batting.
 Share 4h ago 08.16 EDT Thanks Rob. Afternoon/evening everyone . How to follow that, both as a batter and an OBOer? You can’t, frankly. Sri Lanka must be mightily sick of bowling to England – and it must be said they didn’t do it very well in Harry Brook’s Pindi playground, sorely lacking a fifth bowler after the four main ones sputtered. You’d assume this one’s done and dusted but there are bowlers and batters with cases to make, so let’s see.
 Share 4h ago 08.11 EDT My head is spinning. I feel like Dasun Shanaka (6-0-74-0), so I’m going to hand over to Tom Davies for the runchase (sic).
 Thanks for your company, what day are you?
 Share Updated at  08.16 EDT 4h ago 08.09 EDT Sri Lanka’s fifth bowler, a combination of Shanaka, Mendis and Liyanage, finished with figures of 10-0-123-1 . But that wicket came from the last ball of the innings, so they had the last laugh.
 Share 5h ago 08.05 EDT Well, this piece was well timed 
 Golden bat or ball: does cricket need an equivalent to the Ballon d’Or? | Taha Hashim Read more And this piece is well worth a read too.
 The Spin | Writing a book with Chris Woakes showed the inner steel of the nicest man in cricket Read more Share Updated at  08.18 EDT 5h ago 08.02 EDT Harry Brook vs the record books
 Brook made 202 from 116 balls with 21 fours and 10 sixes. He was 13 from 24 at one stage, so he hammered* 189 from the last 92.
 His double-century came from 114 balls , the quickest in ODI history. The previous fastest was Shubman Gill, who needed 117 balls against West Indies in Guwahati last month.
 Brook made the first ODI double-century by an England batter. He romped past England’s previous highest score, Ben Stokes’ 182 not out against New Zealand in 2023.
 England 429-4 is the highest score in an ODI in Pakistan.
 England hit 296 from the last 25 overs of the innings.
 * Actually, that’s the wrong word because so many of his runs came behind square through the deftest of wristwork and placement 
 Share Updated at  08.21 EDT 5h ago 07.58 EDT 50 overs: England 429-4 (Jacks 66) Right, what the hell was that?
 Before any of us try to answer that question, we need to go through the records. Nurse, the Wisdens!
 “Well,” writes Eddy Nason, “that’s ruined his average.”
 View image in fullscreen Will Jacks congratulates his captian. Photograph: Farooq Naeem/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  08.08 EDT 5h ago 07.58 EDT WICKET! England 429-4 (Brook c Arachchiage b Liyanage 202)
 Brook slashes the last ball of the innings to short third and walks off to a standing ovation from an open-mouthed England balcony.
 Share Updated at  08.07 EDT 5h ago 07.56 EDT Harry Brook smashes the fastest-ever ODI double-century!
 Janith Liyanage is brought back for the final over. Imagine his internal monlogue when he realised Kusal Mendis was looking in his direction. Brook, on 186 at the start of the over, blazes the first ball over extra cover for his tenth six.
 Brook wheezes back for consecutive twos. He’s 196 not out, three balls remaining. And he’s done it! He premeditates a ramp for four to reach 200 from 114 balls! Genius? Nah, we need a new word.
 View image in fullscreen Harry Brook raises his bat skyward, celebrating his double century Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/Reuters Share Updated at  08.15 EDT 5h ago 07.52 EDT Harry Brook smashes England's highest ODI score!
 49th over: England 413-3 (Brook 186, Jacks 66) Madushanka has the misfortune of bowling the penultimate over Jacks bullets a six through the fielder at long off. England have scored 400 for the third time since Harry Brook took over as captain.
 Don’t bother making that the headline. Two balls later, Brook times a low full toss from Madushanka for six to break Ben Stokes’ record for the highest ODI score by an England batter. Stokes made 182 not out against New Zealand in 2023, but that’s all ancient history now.
 Brook is dropped off the last ball , a tough running chance at mid-on. He takes a single to keep the strike, which means the double century is on!
 Share Updated at  08.15 EDT 5h ago 07.47 EDT Quick question Does anyone know what day this is?
 Share 5h ago 07.47 EDT 48th over: England 397-3 (Brook 177, Jacks 59) Jacks violates Shanaka over long off to bring up the highest ODI score in Pakistan . Another full ball is pumped for six, this time over wide long on. Mercy.
 Jacks smears a full toss for four to bring up a 24-ball fifty , then belts another full bunger through extra cover for four. This is carnage, redefined. Sri Lanka’s fifth bowler has gone for 111 in nine overs.
 Share Updated at  08.15 EDT 5h ago 07.44 EDT 47th over: England 373-3 (Brook 177, Jacks 36) Malinga almost nails a wide delivery to Brook. Almost: Brook walks across, gets down on one knee and laps it past leg stump for four. Sorry, what?
 Shanaka doesn’t know what day it is or what name his parents gave him, never mind what length to bowl. A very short ball is pummelled over extra cover for four more by Brook, who is now 177 not out from 106 balls. He’s one hit away from the England record.
 After the Pakistan defeat on Tuesday, Brook said England needed to put more pressure on the opposition bowlers. Walk the talk? He’s running the bloody marathon!
 Share Updated at  08.14 EDT 5h ago 07.38 EDT 46th over: England 362-3 (Brook 168, Jacks 35) Brook uses his rubber wrists to whip Fernando behind square on the leg side for four. Yeah, fours are good but languid sixes down the ground are better. Brook launches his eighth six before taking a single to keep strike.
 Wherever he is in the world, I hope Kevin Pietersen is watching this.
 “I do remember the 1979 World Cup final, I’m afraid,” says John Stedman. “Wasn’t that the one when Clive Lloyd, one of the finest fielders to have ever played the game dropped Geoff Boycott, with disastrous consequences - for England?”
 In defence of Sir Geoffrey, England would have lost that game 10 times out of 10 once West Indies reached 286-9. (Also, it was Beefy who encouraged Boycott and Mike Brearley to continue at the same tempo, but that’s another story .)
